title: GRACE THAT STILL TAKES SIN SERIOUSLY

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord replied to Moses, "If her father had spit in her face, would she not have been in disgrace for seven days? Confine her outside the camp for seven days; after that she can be brought back." So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on till she was brought back. — Num 12:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God answers Moses' prayer — Miriam will be healed and restored. But there is still a consequence: seven days outside the camp. Here we see two truths held together beautifully. God is merciful, and God takes sin seriously. Grace does not mean sin has no consequences; it means God provides a way back.

Those seven days outside the camp would have given Miriam time to reflect, to let the reality of her sin sink in, and to return with a changed heart. Consequences are not always punishment for its own sake; often they are God's tool to teach and reshape us. A love that never allowed any consequence would not be true love at all.

There is a tender detail in the last line: "the people did not move on till she was brought back." The whole nation waited for her. Even in her discipline, Miriam was not cast off or forgotten. The community paused for one restored sister. That is the heart of God — He disciplines, but He does not discard.

For us, this points to the greater restoration found in Christ. Sin puts us "outside the camp," separated from God. But Jesus, as Hebrews tells us, suffered "outside the camp" to bring us back in. He took the place of exclusion so that we could be welcomed home. God's discipline always aims at restoration, and in Christ that homecoming is sure.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you accept that God's love sometimes includes consequences?
2. How have hard seasons been used by God to reshape your heart?
3. What does it mean to you that Jesus went "outside the camp" for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your discipline flows from love and always aims at bringing me home. Help me to receive correction humbly, and thank You that Christ went outside the camp so I could be welcomed in. Amen.
